title: Paranormal society shares about Superior's unseen residents
excerpt: The Duluth Paranormal Society has spent a lot of time investigating locations in Superior and will share stories this spooky season.
content:
SUPERIOR — A paranormal investigative society is hosting a series of events in Superior just in time for spooky season.

The Duluth Paranormal Society has been investigating the Duluth-Superior region since the group formed in fall 2012. According to co-director Chera Pufahl, the team has investigated several locations in Superior.

"Primarily private residences as well as several businesses," Pufahl said. "We have recorded disembodied voices and unexplained noises that remained unresolved despite our efforts to debunk them."

Each October, society representatives give a free talk about their investigations at the Superior Public Library. This year's talk is at 5:30 p.m. Oct. 20.

"It's been a pretty popular event," Pufahl said.

A collaboration with Fairlawn Mansion was even more popular. The society conducted a series of paranormal investigation tours Sept. 26 that sold out in advance.

The group has investigated the mansion several times.

"Our investigations there have produced several intriguing experiences, including unexplained odors, noises from empty rooms, and a light moving across the floor of one room — none of which we could debunk," Pufahl said.

On Oct. 24, Pufahl will team up with the Douglas County Historical Society for "Haunted Superior: Dark History Revealed" at 1101 John. Ave. The talk starts at 5 p.m. and tickets are $10.

"Our researcher is taking an in-depth look at Douglas County’s history for events that may be associated with local paranormal activity or hauntings," Pufahl said. "DCHS has been extremely helpful with this research, and we hope to uncover some intriguing local history."

The night will include artifacts and archival records from the historical society's collection to help illustrate.

Teri Cadeau is a reporter for the Superior Telegram. Originally from the Iron Range, Cadeau has worked for several community newspapers in the Duluth area, including the Duluth Budgeteer News, Western Weekly, Weekly Observer, Lake County News-Chronicle, Duluth News Tribune and occasionally, the Cloquet Pine Journal. When not working, she's an avid reader, crafter, dancer, trivia fanatic and cribbage player.
